title: pricing-packaging-scratchpad-isaac-2026-03-04
content:
Notes: pricing + unit economics (back-of-envelope)

Context / goal:
- Quick scratch to validate feasible hosted API rates and reserved capacity tiers. Not final - oriented to understand gross margins and break-even on reserved contracts.

Assumptions (rough):
- Avg prompt tokens (in): 300
- Avg completion tokens (out): 150
- Total tokens per call: 450
- Calls per month per small app: 50k -> monthly tokens = 22.5M

Infra cost assumptions (per 1k tokens):
- Small/quantized model (7B-ish): $0.0015 / 1k tokens
- Medium model (13-33B): $0.003 / 1k tokens
- Large (70B+): $0.01 / 1k tokens
(These are inclusive of instance amortization, GPU power, NVMe, networking, ops overhead - very rough)

Customer price examples (hosted API):
- Hobby tier: $0.04 / 1k tokens
- Startup tier: $0.02 / 1k tokens (volume discounted)
- Scale / enterprise: custom, e.g., $0.008 - $0.015 / 1k tokens depending on commitment and SLA

Example unit economics (medium model):
- Infra cost = $0.003 / 1k
- Customer price = $0.02 / 1k -> gross margin ~ 85%
- For a small app (22.5M tokens/mo): revenue = $450; infra cost = $67.5 -> gross = $382.5

Reserved capacity (Dedicated) rough thinking:
- Sell committed GPU-hrs/month. Example SKU: 1x A10-equivalent pool = 720 GPU-hrs/mo. Price to customer: $7,000/mo for predictable baseline (example).
- Map to expected throughput: assume sustained serving throughput = 7k tokens/sec (depends on batching). Monthly tokens ~ 7k * 3600 * 24 * 30 = ~18.1B tokens. Implied cost/customer ~ $0.00038 / 1k tokens (~cheap) but needs calibration: utilization, multi-tenant overhead, model mix, memory limits.

Tier ideas (hosted):
- Free / dev: 100k tokens/mo included, throttled QPS, no SLA
- Hobby: $5/mo + 100k tokens included, $0.05 / 1k overage (7B quantized recommended)
- Startup: $250/mo + 5M tokens included, $0.02 / 1k overage, priority support
- Business: $2k/mo + 50M tokens, $0.012 / 1k overage, SLOs, audit logs
- Enterprise: committed PO / reserved pools, custom pricing, uplift for SLA, PII handling, VPC

Bundling notes:
- Add-ons: embeddings priced differently (embedding model infra cost higher per token? but shorter sequences) - suggested: $0.03 / 1k tokens for embeddings (or per-embedding unit pricing).
- Rate limiting / QoS as a pack: cheaper per-token if customer accepts best-effort routing and lower priority during bursts.

Sensitivity checks / back-of-envelope tests:
- If infra cost for medium model doubles (i.e., $0.006 / 1k), Startup tier margin drops to 70% - still OK but reserved capacity becomes more attractive for high-volume customers.
- If average tokens/call increases to 1k total, monthly bills scale linearly; consider burst protection + prefix caching to reduce effective cost.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate infra cost estimates with infra team (Priya) - need real cost per 1k tokens by model family & region.
- Run simulation in price-sim repo for mixed workloads (chat-heavy vs embedding-heavy). Link: github PR above.
- Decide embedding unit metric vs token-based metric (embedding-per-call vs tokens).
- Map reserved pool pricing to our Dedicated SKU cost and target utilization (70-80% recommended).

Quick numbers to present to leadership (slide):
- Hosted baseline price: $0.02 / 1k (medium model) -> ~80% gross margin at current infra assumptions
- Hobby plan to capture developer growth: $5/mo + cheap overage (elastic)
- Dedicated: price per GPU-month that yields 30-40% margin at 70% util given multi-model ops costs

Notes to self:
- Keep product simple: 3 hosted tiers + clear dedicated entry. Avoid >10 skus.
- Run A/B on overage price elasticity for startups (0.01 -> 0.03 range).
- Check competitive public pricing (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) and make sure we have lower-latency / higher-throughput value props for same price band.

End of scratch.
